**Resubmitted: deviation (T4C), fallback target, two operations — both validated (`ok:true`, minimality clean).**

Repairs made in response to the verifier:

1. **Element 3 / Customer-right deterministic failure — now express operative words (Op 1, §4.1 / p0024).** I accepted that the symmetric "terminated by either Party hereto" cannot bear the asymmetric reading, and that the "Such notice shall specify the date" sentence would let HDI pick any date 90+ days out. The renewal proviso now reads: terminable "upon ninety (90) days written notice by the Company at any time or by HDI only effective at the expiration of the then-current term." One replacement carries all three notice-side elements — Customer right express and at-will on 90 days, HDI confined to term expiry, 90-day notice retained for both — instead of resting the position on the margin comment.

2. **Minimality / customer-favourable language preserved (Op 2, §4.2(a) / p0026).** Redrafted as a ceiling rather than a substitution: "the lesser of (i) the aggregate Net Sales for the twelve (12) months preceding the Termination Date less $800,000, divided by two, and (ii) the payments due to HDI under Section 3.1 for the three (3) months preceding the Termination Date." This keeps the existing netting, so we still owe nothing at or below $800,000 of trailing Net Sales — the earlier draft would have created a ~$50,000 liability there.

3. **Vestigial text resolved.** Because the netting calculation survives inside limb (i), §4.2(b)'s "less than or equal to zero" mechanic remains fully operative; no offset implication is created.

4. **Scope discipline.** The breach carve-out sits outside the fallback checklist, so it is raised in the comment (aligned to §1.6's "without penalty") rather than drafted into the operative text. Preferred level remains unattempted — there are no prepaid fees to refund under this revenue-share model.
